ghEnglish._enabledNote: 20 Oct 2026: the cached F5 Kafui lines play first; a line not cached waits only firstWaitMs, then the phone's own Kafui voice (models/ondevice/eng/tts, chain 'ghvoice') speaks it. false = on-device Kafui only.
ghEnglish._note: 19 Oct 2026: the Kafui Dey English voice from the language Space is the default English voice. A CPU line takes ~24 s when the Space GPU is busy, so a first sentence gets 12 s (then the phone voice speaks), and the app's fixed lines are kept on disk (HttpProviders.TtsDiskCache.keepsEnglish) so they play at once after one slow fetch.
ghEnglish._waitMsNote: 29 Oct 2026: a network English voice can have its own waits (first sentence / each next one). Gemini's Kore MAKES every line: one short sentence took 4.3-4.8 s from the laptop at the camp (the shared 150 ms cancelled it every time on the Infinix). Kafui on the Space keeps 150 ms (cached lines only). With Kore the reply starts ~4.5 s later than the phone's own Kafui voice; lines the app says every time are kept on the phone after the first fetch and play at once.

voiceLayer._note: gh_mixed (owner's choice 2026-09-29, the default) = English: Android SpeechRecognizer + system TTS; Twi: UG HCI Lab ASR (on-device Twi Whisper fallback) + HCI Lab TTS — one recognizer per listen, chosen by the language setting ('speak Twi' / 'speak English'). builtin_en = Android SpeechRecognizer + system TTS, English only (SherpaAsr and the HCI Lab language layer are not built). ghana = MicCapture + HybridAsr (sherpa Whisper-tiny + UG HCI Lab ASR) + RoutingTts (HCI Lab Twi TTS). Only VoiceEngine.init reads this (voice/io/VoiceLayer.kt). The secure step never starts the system recognizer: the user taps Done.

systemSpeech._note: component: a flattened ComponentName to pin one recognizer (only if the A20e test shows the default misbehaves). ownCue: beforeStart = our tone then the recognizer; none = the recognizer's own tone only. silenceExtras: SPEECH_INPUT_* hints (2.5 s / 2 s since 2026-09-29, after 'it stops listening early') — many stock recognizers ignore them, so patience is also built by re-listening. freshPerListen: a new SpeechRecognizer per listen so a stopped session's late callbacks can't reach the next one.

bargeIn._note: B-07 OFF by default: on the Galaxy A20e (2026-09-28) the echo canceller let the phone's own TTS through, so every long reply interrupted itself (the reply played on the media stream, which the platform AEC does not take as its echo reference). With duplex on, a barge-in reply plays on the voice-communication path (MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION + loudspeaker, call volume matched to the media volume) so the AEC can cancel it; never during a call or with a headset. Turn enabled on per device after checking; SelfEcho still guards against it.

reading._note: A screen reading is spoken in parts of about partSeconds at the user's speech rate (was a fixed 480 characters, ~30 s), each ending 'There's more — say continue'; the mic re-opens after each part for 'continue' or 'stop'.

fillers._note: Spoken in the reply voice (the phone's engine). Twi is empty on purpose: the old Twi phrasings were never verified by a native speaker and the English engine reads Twi badly, so a Twi session plays the progress tone. Add verified phrases here.
fillers._en_note: Owner, 3 Nov 2026: 'some of them don't fit where they're kept at all' — 'Let me check/find that for you' and 'let me take a look' assumed a lookup and were said before jokes, chat, 'yes' and sends. Every line here must fit ANY request.

wake._engine_doc: 8 Nov 2026 (owner): the wake word is 'Nexus' ('Hey Nexus', 'Nexus', anything that mentions Nexus). engine 'kws' = sherpa-onnx keyword spotter (voice/NexusSpotter, assets/wakeword/kws, no training); 'oww' = the trained 'Hey Tɛkyerɛma' head above (bar/marginalBelow are for it). Setting 'oww' needs ui/Brand.kt WAKE back to 'Hey Tɛkyerɛma' too. kws threshold/boost: 2 Nov spike kws_v2 at 0.05/2.0 → 87% clean, 80% at 20 dB, 73% at 10 dB, 0 false accepts in 2.31 h of Ghanaian speech; lower threshold or higher boost = wakes more easily.
